page: Amazon Web Services r8a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates with an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores placing in the top 10%. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank in the top tier, alongside small-model LLM inference speeds. Multi-core stress-ng performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations on Redis fall within the average range.

The high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1 makes this instance qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The absence of local storage means all storage must be network-attached, which may impact I/O-heavy operations despite the 8 Gbps network baseline. It is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, including database operations, caching layers, text and image processing, and small-scale language model inference.
